raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Depends on #2123.

SM107 half D64 dense unsplit plans currently run a two-slab prefill body even when every live query row fits in one slab. Select the existing physical-D64 single-Q body for N128/CGA1 plans when Q length times the packed group fits 128 rows. The module is compiled for the actual SM107 target.

Keep longer queries, N64, CGA2, THD, paged, additive bias, KV masks and prefolded-scale handling on their existing paths. No public capability, knob domain or heuristic policy changes. Both graph and standalone execution retain the same bindings, output precision and workspace contract.

Validation: host route regressions fail before the change (4 failed / 7 passed) and pass afterward (11 passed), including boundary and feature controls. On SM107, 62 graph/standalone replay-and-rebind tests pass: 20 new unsplit cases plus the existing split and packing controls. Two scoped memcheck cases pass with zero errors. Coverage includes FP16/BF16, partial GQA, asymmetric widths, masks/sinks, both Stats log bases, the 128-row boundary and a 129-row prefill control. Scoped pre-commit passes.

Output width, Stats mode, sink handling and zero unsplit workspace were checked. These are host checks, not GPU execution. A clean isolated merge with f4639c3d passed 861 host tests and the same 460 route checks. All 12 changed files in CI match that merge. Reviewed the five-file delta since #2123's corrected head. Kernel bodies and reduction loops are unchanged. The selected module retains physical D64, one Q slab, half output and unsplit Stats/sink handling; SM107 does not enable the separate early-Q or quadrant paths. Bias, KV-mask, prefolded, THD, paged, N64 and CGA2 boundaries remain intact. The SM107 entrypoint includes 20 new graph/standalone replay and rebind cases, including optional Stats, both log bases, masks/sinks, partial packing and the 129-row prefill control. Reused the author's current-head CI request and completed release metadata.

Limitations: No independent native SM107 execution, sanitizer, repeatability or performance measurement was performed. The author's native tests are separate evidence; CI remains pending. Source and host checks establish the selected route and binding contract, not a native speedup or bitwise equivalence between the two kernel bodies.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
